text: dsh-terminal-shell 是面向 Windows DSH 的终端切换插件，在设置的通用面板提供终端 Shell 选项，并按会话把终端工具切换为本机 Git Bash 或 cmd.exe，也可保留默认 PowerShell。它会为 bash 提供路径发现与配置，并可调整会话终端相关选项。适合希望在 Windows DSH 会话中使用 Git Bash 或命令提示符的用户；bash 需要本机 shell 环境，不需要 API 密钥。

dsh-terminal-shell lets Windows DSH sessions use Git Bash or cmd.exe, with PowerShell kept as the default. A General settings row exposes the choice and shell options. Git Bash requires a local installation; no API key is needed.
dsh-terminal-shell 的功能「会话终端切换」：为新建的 Windows DSH 会话选择 Git Bash 或 cmd.exe，并将对应终端工具装入该会话；默认 pwsh 设置会保留原有终端。通过通用设置选择方言。
dsh-terminal-shell 的功能「终端设置面板」：在设置 → 通用提供终端选择和方言对应的路径、沙箱策略等控件；bash 路径可由程序发现或手动指定。用户在面板中调整配置。
dsh-terminal-shell README · Introduction：

dsh-terminal-shell README · dsh-terminal-shell：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

On Windows, choose which shell sits behind the terminal tool the agent invokes — **PowerShell** (`pwsh`), the **local Git Bash** (`bash`), or **`cmd.exe`** (`cmd`). One switch under **Settings → General**, applied to **new sessions only**: no preset file edited, no global `ctx.shell` takeover.

`v0.2.1` · MIT · Windows (DSH Desktop / Web shell) · `engines.node` `>=22` · `engines.dsh` `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`

dsh-terminal-shell README · Why this plugin：DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 ships **one** terminal per platform, and on Windows that is PowerShell: the bash family is disabled by `!!js process.platform === 'win32'` assertions in `dsh-base`, and `ctx.shell` is a **single-instance** service (a second registration throws `service "shell" has been registered`). A Windows session therefore has no bash executor and no `bash` tool.

The common ways to change that each cost something:

dsh-terminal-shell README · Why this plugin：| Approach | Cost / limitation |
|---|---|
| Patch the platform assertion in `dsh-base` or the profile | Edits first-party composition; affects one plane only; needs a restart |
| Write your own PTY / tool from scratch | Re-implements a 60 KB+ tool contract; drifts from official behavior |
| Drop in a **global** shell replacer | Changes **every** session, even ones that never asked; collides with the host executor |
dsh-terminal-shell README · Why this plugin：**This plugin does per-session isolated replacement instead** — that is its point:

dsh-terminal-shell README · Why this plugin：- **Only new sessions, and only the ones you switch.** The executor is composed into each new session's own `isolate('shell')` subtree; the host plane and all other sessions stay untouched, and uninstalling leaves no residue.
- **Three dialects, one switch, and install changes nothing.** `dialect` defaults to `pwsh`, so out of the box behavior is identical to the official one.
- **No pinned executable paths.** Git Bash is discovered at runtime on each machine, so the same repo works everywhere.
- **Covers the sidebar too.** An extra option makes the sidebar **New Terminal → Shell** menu launch this machine's Git Bash instead of WSL's `bash` — something the stock menu cannot do.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Why this plugin：Beyond Git Bash, the **`cmd`** dialect is there for when you want Windows-native behavior instead of a POSIX layer: exact `cmd.exe` batch semantics (`.cmd` scripts, `%VAR%` expansion, native pipes and redirection) with no MSYS dependency. It is a one-shot executor reusing the official tool contract, so the model can drive plain `cmd` exactly as the OS runs it.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Why this plugin：First-party behavior — timeouts, output spill, abort classification, background jobs, `sandbox_permissions` escalation, session cwd, tool cards, exit-code markers — is inherited from or reuses the official implementation.

dsh-terminal-shell README · How it works：On `agent/created`, the plugin composes everything into the new session only:

```
shellCtx = agentCtx.isolate('shell')                 // this agent's private shell realm
shellCtx.plugin(GitBashExecutor, {...})              // executor visible only in this subtree
shellCtx.plugin(ToolBash, {...})                     // the bash tool lands in the agent's own layer
agentCtx.tools.restrict({ deny: ['pwsh'] })          // filters only INHERITED tools

dsh-terminal-shell README · How it works：`restrict` only hides the *inherited* layer, so it removes the preset's `pwsh` without touching the `bash` this layer registered (`cmd` denies `pwsh` + `bash`). All steps are released in reverse when the session ends, and a mid-way failure rolls back. New sessions only — tool catalogs are assembled at session creation and cannot be swapped at runtime.

dsh-terminal-shell README · How it works：

> The **Terminal shell** row (bash dialect). The highlighted last line, **Sidebar terminal**, is the option that makes the sidebar New Terminal use this machine's Git Bash. ---

dsh-terminal-shell README · Install / enable：**Prerequisites:** Windows; DSH Desktop / Web shell `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`; for `bash` a local Git for Windows / MSYS2 / Cygwin; for `cmd` nothing extra.

Install it like any other profile plugin — either way works:

dsh-terminal-shell README · Install / enable：- **In the app:** open **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste the package name `dsh-terminal-shell` (or this repository's URL, or a local folder path), click **Install**, then **Enable now**.
- **CLI:** `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-terminal-shell` — it runs pnpm inside the profile and registers the bundle automatically. A GitHub URL or a local path works too.

The package ships its own `dsh.bundle.patch`, which inserts exactly one row and pins no executable path:

dsh-terminal-shell README · Install / enable：```yaml
- insert:
    - id: terminal-shell
      name: dsh-terminal-shell
      disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'

**Restart DSH after install or upgrade** — a row inserted at runtime only enters the composition tree; `apply` is not called until restart. `dialect` stays `pwsh` until you change it.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Enabling：After restart, **Settings → General** shows a new **Terminal shell** row at the bottom (`settings.general.item`, id `terminal-shell`, order `60`, locale `terminal-shell`). Pick a dialect there; each control maps one-to-one to a field in [Configuration reference](#configuration-reference).

dsh-terminal-shell README · Usage：**Row layout.** Matches the official General rows: label + one explanatory line + a control on the right, official design tokens, theme-aware. **Order:** `bash` = path → sandbox policy → minimal mode → **Sidebar terminal**; `cmd` = path → sandbox policy → minimal mode → code page; `pwsh` shows only the dialect row.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Usage：**Switching the dialect triggers a scan** — choosing a shell *is* the scan; there is no separate detect button. The path field is a plain input you can type into, and becomes a dropdown when a scan finds several candidates. A still-valid chosen path is never overwritten, a failed write or scan retries once automatically, and mounting does no scan and no config write.

**Sandbox policy** (`confinedPolicy` for `bash`, `cmdConfinedPolicy` for `cmd`):

dsh-terminal-shell README · Usage：| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `Bypass the sandbox` (`unconfined`) | Under the restricted Windows tier, launch directly without `ctx.sandbox.confine()`; succeeds at once but the command is **not** file-sandboxed |
| `Request permission` (`escalate`) | Enter the sandbox the official way; an MSYS launch failure becomes the official escalation prompt, retried with `sandbox_permissions: danger-full-access` |

dsh-terminal-shell README · Usage：Defaults differ on purpose: **`bash` defaults to `unconfined`** because MSYS2 / Git Bash cannot start under a restricted Windows token (`NtCreateDirectoryObject` → `0xC0000022`), so `escalate` would fail once before every approval; **`cmd` defaults to `escalate`** because `cmd.exe` starts fine under a restricted token, so the sandbox is both safe and working. Approval is handled entirely by the first-party tool; the plugin only classifies MSYS launch failures as `denied`.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Usage：**Minimal mode** (`minimalMode`, `bash` only): the official `minimal` preset has a persistent pwsh shell, so a `minimal` session needs a decision — `leave` (keep pwsh), `oneshot` (switch to a one-shot bash, default), or `variant` (also register a persistent `minimal-gitbash` preset; official `minimal` untouched; removed automatically when unreferenced; must be re-chosen per new session).
dsh-terminal-shell README · Usage：**Console code page** (`cmdCodePage`, `cmd` only): runs `chcp <codePage>>nul` first; default `65001` (UTF-8), the only value that keeps non-ASCII output intact.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Usage：**Bash discovery order** (when `bashPath` is empty): explicit `bashPath` → `bashCandidates` → registry `HKLM\SOFTWARE\GitForWindows` `InstallPath` → `%ProgramFiles%\Git` and friends → MSYS2 → Cygwin → back-derived from `git.exe` on PATH. **WSL is hard-excluded** (`System32\bash.exe`, `WindowsApps\bash.exe` are a different OS/filesystem). Discovery only stats the filesystem plus one async `reg.exe query`; it never spawns `bash --version`.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Usage：**cmd discovery** (when `cmdPath` is empty): `cmdPath` → `%ComSpec%` → `%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe`; no disk scan. A `cmdPath` that is not `cmd.exe` is treated as unset.

**Child PATH**: toolchain `bin` → `usr\bin` → `bin` → `usr\local\bin` → `extraPath` → host PATH, so MSYS2 tools win but native `node` / `python` survive.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Configuration reference：Every field is `.volatile()` and surfaces through the official `configForms`; the row edits some directly, the rest can be set in the profile patch.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Configuration reference：| patch key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dialect` | `'pwsh' \| 'bash' \| 'cmd'` | `'pwsh'` | Terminal dialect |
| `bashPath` | `string` | `''` | Explicit `bash.exe` path; empty = auto-discover |
| `bashCandidates` | `string[]` | `[]` | Extra discovery roots / explicit paths, tried before the built-ins |
| `autoDiscover` | `boolean` | `true` | Auto-discover at session assembly when `bashPath` is empty |
| `discoverTimeoutMs` | `number` | `1500` | One discovery's time bound |
| `loginShell` | `boolean` | `false` | Pass `-l` to read the login profile |
| `extraPath` | `string[]` | `[]` | Extra dirs appended to the child PATH |
| `pythonUtf8` | `boolean` | `true` | Export `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` |
| `confinedPolicy` | `'unconfined' \| 'escalate'` | `'unconfined'` | `bash` behavior under the restricted tier |
| `cmdPath` | `string` | `''` | Explicit `cmd.exe` path; empty = `%ComSpec%` fallback |
| `cmdCodePage` | `number` | `65001` | `chcp` code page |
| `cmdConfinedPolicy` | `'escalate' \| 'unconfined'` | `'escalate'` | `cmd` behavior under the restricted tier |
| `minimalMode` | `'leave' \| 'oneshot' \| 'variant

dsh-terminal-shell README · Configuration reference：> `confinedPolicy` / `cmdConfinedPolicy` accept **only** `unconfined` / `escalate` (0.2.1 removed `fail`; writing `fail` fails schema validation — see [Diagnostics](#diagnostics-and-troubleshooting)).

dsh-terminal-shell README · Uninstall：Uninstall it the same way you installed it: in **Plugins** open the plugin and click **Uninstall** (or run `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-terminal-shell`), then **restart**; new sessions return to the official tool. No global residue (no `ctx.shell`, no preset edits, nothing written to the install dir). Sessions already opened under Git Bash / cmd keep running it (tools are fixed at creation). The `variant` preset unregisters itself with the plugin.

---

dsh-terminal-shell README · Stopgap status：DSH has no built-in terminal / shell selection today, so **until the official capability lands this plugin is the stopgap** — it uses the officially shipped executors and tools to swap the terminal of new Windows sessions, and `confinedPolicy` under the restricted tier is part of the same temporary wiring. Once an official equivalent exists, disable the plugin (uninstall it and restart) and new sessions return to the official terminal tool. The plugin never edits the DSH install directory, any preset, or the global `ctx.shell` — its configuration lives only in the current profile's patch layer, so uninstalling needs no cleanup — with one deliberate exception: `minimalMode: variant` registers a **new preset** (`minimal-gitbash`) while the official `minimal` stays untouched, and that preset vanishes once no session references it (see Usage).

dsh-terminal-shell README · cmd dialect limitations：`cmd` is the only dialect **not** built on the official bash tool (`src/cmd/tool.ts` is a verbatim port); every constraint below comes from `cmd.exe` / batch semantics:

dsh-terminal-shell README · cmd dialect limitations：1. **One-shot batch** — each call is a fresh temporary `.cmd`; `pause`, `set /p`, or any interactive prompt hangs until timeout.
2. **No echo** — `cmd.exe /q` disables command echo, so only the command's own output returns; `@echo on` cannot override `/q`.
3. **Batch placeholders** — `%0` / `%1`–`%9` / `%*` / `%~dp0` point at the plugin's internal script, not your command line; use `%CD%` for the working directory.
4. **`%VAR%` expands per batch rules** — a `set` on the same line is not visible to a new variable on that line.
5. **Encoding** — non-ASCII output depends on the console code page (`cmdCodePage`, default `65001`).
6. **`cmdPath` only accepts `cmd.exe`** — anything else is rejected by the client and by discovery; empty falls back to `%ComSpec%` → `%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe`.
7. **No persistent PTY** — `cmd` has no persistent terminal and does not replace `minimal`'s persistent shell.
8. **Sandbox-denied marker may be missing** — on Chinese Windows the denial message is GBK, so the provider's English signatures may not match; the sandbox still applies and the plugin does not fake the verdict.

dsh-terminal-shell README · cmd dialect limitations：Each execution writes a `cmd-<uuid>.cmd` into the executor's own scratch dir (cwd set to that dir, invoked by bare name) because `cmd.exe` cannot take a quoting-safe multi-line command as an argument; a `cd /d "<cwd>"` guard prevents silently running in the scratch dir, and the script's exit code is left as the last command's own.

---

dsh-terminal-shell README · Diagnostics and troubleshooting：One line per session to `%TEMP%\dsh-terminal-shell.log` (override with `DSH_TERMINAL_TOOL_DIAG_FILE`), e.g. `ok ... bash=... source=registry` or `skip ... reason=bash-not-found`. `reason` values include `not-win32` / `dialect-pwsh` / `already-replaced` / `bash-not-found` / `cmd-not-found` / `minimal-left` / `mount-failed` / `cmd-script-failed`.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Diagnostics and troubleshooting：| Symptom | Action |
|---|---|
| Changed the setting, no effect | Tools are fixed at session creation — only a **new session** picks it up |
| No new tool after restart | Fully quit and restart the host, then create a **new** session |
| `bash-not-found` / `cmd-not-found` | Set `bashPath` / `cmdPath` explicitly |
| Startup fails with `confinedPolicy: fail` | `fail` is no longer valid — use `unconfined` or `escalate` |

dsh-terminal-shell README · Diagnostics and troubleshooting：The listener is fully defensive: any exception only goes to the log and never fails session creation.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Development：Build from source:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/road-kid/dsh-terminal-shell.git
cd dsh-terminal-shell
npm install
npm run build        # esbuild → lib/index.js, lib/client.js, lib/pty.js

Source map:

```
src/index.ts      plugin entry: apply / Config / agent events / capability probe
src/config.ts     schemastery Config (volatile) + per-session snapshot
src/discover.ts   Git Bash discovery (incl. WSL exclusion)
src/paths.ts      path arithmetic, validation, PATH composition

dsh-terminal-shell README · Development：`npm run typecheck` · `npm run build` (esbuild → `lib/index.js`, `lib/client.js`, `lib/pty.js`) · `npm run check` (runs all: contractcheck 19, clientsmoke 8, selftest 51, rowselftest 19, rendertest 21, cmdunit 37, integration 13, cmdtest 14, ptytests 3).

dsh-terminal-shell README · Development：First-party `@deepseek-ai/*` packages stay **external** at build time (inlining would duplicate service classes and break cordis's `instanceof` / identity checks); the client keeps `react` and the official atoms external too. Type declarations are hand-written `.d.ts` to avoid dragging in the first-party type graph.

Architecture, decision rationale, and deviations from the official implementation are documented in [`docs/DESIGN.md`](docs/DESIGN.md).

---

dsh-terminal-shell README · Compatibility：Windows only (`disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'`). DSH Desktop / Web shell. `engines.node >=22`, `engines.dsh >=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` is a `peerDependency`, external at build time. Coexists with a persistent-terminal bundle (e.g. `experimental-terminal-bundle`): the two registries and `terminal_*` tools never read or write each other's state.
dsh-terminal-shell README · Coexisting with other plugins：Footprint (all prefixed `terminal-shell` / `dsh-terminal-shell`; the first loader wins on conflict):

dsh-terminal-shell README · Coexisting with other plugins：| Surface | Name |
|---|---|
| Settings row slot | `settings.general.item`, id `terminal-shell`, order `60` |
| Locale namespace | `terminal-shell` |
| Bundle row id | `terminal-shell` |
| Host routes | `/api/dsh-terminal-shell/state`, `/api/dsh-terminal-shell/discover` |
| In-session tools | `bash` replaces `bash`, hides `pwsh`; `cmd` adds `cmd`, hides `pwsh` and `bash` (replaced session only) |

dsh-terminal-shell README · Coexisting with other plugins：- **Writes no global state** — no `ctx.shell`, no preset edits, nothing in the install dir, no pinned path. With `sidebarBash: gitbash` it hands the core `terminal-controller` an in-memory `config.shell` override (never persisted); `system` leaves it untouched.
- **Another plugin that also replaces the session's `bash`** (for example another Git Bash plugin): both want it; this plugin skips when it finds a `bash` already in scope (`already-replaced`) but cannot tell whose. Install just one.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Uninstall：Uninstall it the same way you installed it: in **Plugins** open the plugin and click **Uninstall** (or run `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-terminal-shell`), then **restart**; new sessions return to the official tool. No global residue (no `ctx.shell`, no preset edits, nothing written to the install dir). Sessions already opened under Git Bash / cmd keep running it (tools are fixed at creation). The `variant` preset unregisters itself with the plugin.

---

dsh-terminal-shell README · Stopgap status：DSH has no built-in terminal / shell selection today, so **until the official capability lands this plugin is the stopgap** — it uses the officially shipped executors and tools to swap the terminal of new Windows sessions, and `confinedPolicy` under the restricted tier is part of the same temporary wiring. Once an official equivalent exists, disable the plugin (uninstall it and restart) and new sessions return to the official terminal tool. The plugin never edits the DSH install directory, any preset, or the global `ctx.shell` — its configuration lives only in the current profile's patch layer, so uninstalling needs no cleanup — with one deliberate exception: `minimalMode: variant` registers a **new preset** (`minimal-gitbash`) while the official `minimal` stays untouched, and that preset vanishes once no session references it (see Usage).

dsh-terminal-shell README · cmd dialect limitations：`cmd` is the only dialect **not** built on the official bash tool (`src/cmd/tool.ts` is a verbatim port); every constraint below comes from `cmd.exe` / batch semantics:

dsh-terminal-shell README · cmd dialect limitations：1. **One-shot batch** — each call is a fresh temporary `.cmd`; `pause`, `set /p`, or any interactive prompt hangs until timeout.
2. **No echo** — `cmd.exe /q` disables command echo, so only the command's own output returns; `@echo on` cannot override `/q`.
3. **Batch placeholders** — `%0` / `%1`–`%9` / `%*` / `%~dp0` point at the plugin's internal script, not your command line; use `%CD%` for the working directory.
4. **`%VAR%` expands per batch rules** — a `set` on the same line is not visible to a new variable on that line.
5. **Encoding** — non-ASCII output depends on the console code page (`cmdCodePage`, default `65001`).
6. **`cmdPath` only accepts `cmd.exe`** — anything else is rejected by the client and by discovery; empty falls back to `%ComSpec%` → `%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe`.
7. **No persistent PTY** — `cmd` has no persistent terminal and does not replace `minimal`'s persistent shell.
8. **Sandbox-denied marker may be missing** — on Chinese Windows the denial message is GBK, so the provider's English signatures may not match; the sandbox still applies and the plugin does not fake the verdict.

dsh-terminal-shell README · cmd dialect limitations：Each execution writes a `cmd-<uuid>.cmd` into the executor's own scratch dir (cwd set to that dir, invoked by bare name) because `cmd.exe` cannot take a quoting-safe multi-line command as an argument; a `cd /d "<cwd>"` guard prevents silently running in the scratch dir, and the script's exit code is left as the last command's own.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Diagnostics and troubleshooting：One line per session to `%TEMP%\dsh-terminal-shell.log` (override with `DSH_TERMINAL_TOOL_DIAG_FILE`), e.g. `ok ... bash=... source=registry` or `skip ... reason=bash-not-found`. `reason` values include `not-win32` / `dialect-pwsh` / `already-replaced` / `bash-not-found` / `cmd-not-found` / `minimal-left` / `mount-failed` / `cmd-script-failed`.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Diagnostics and troubleshooting：| Symptom | Action |
|---|---|
| Changed the setting, no effect | Tools are fixed at session creation — only a **new session** picks it up |
| No new tool after restart | Fully quit and restart the host, then create a **new** session |
| `bash-not-found` / `cmd-not-found` | Set `bashPath` / `cmdPath` explicitly |
| Startup fails with `confinedPolicy: fail` | `fail` is no longer valid — use `unconfined` or `escalate` |

dsh-terminal-shell README · Diagnostics and troubleshooting：The listener is fully defensive: any exception only goes to the log and never fails session creation.

dsh-terminal-shell README · Development：First-party `@deepseek-ai/*` packages stay **external** at build time (inlining would duplicate service classes and break cordis's `instanceof` / identity checks); the client keeps `react` and the official atoms external too. Type declarations are hand-written `.d.ts` to avoid dragging in the first-party type graph.

Architecture, decision rationale, and deviations from the official implementation are documented in [`docs/DESIGN.md`](docs/DESIGN.md).

dsh-terminal-shell README · Compatibility：Windows only (`disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'`). DSH Desktop / Web shell. `engines.node >=22`, `engines.dsh >=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` is a `peerDependency`, external at build time. Coexists with a persistent-terminal bundle (e.g. `experimental-terminal-bundle`): the two registries and `terminal_*` tools never read or write each other's state.
dsh-terminal-shell README · Coexisting with other plugins：Footprint (all prefixed `terminal-shell` / `dsh-terminal-shell`; the first loader wins on conflict):

dsh-terminal-shell README · Coexisting with other plugins：| Surface | Name |
|---|---|
| Settings row slot | `settings.general.item`, id `terminal-shell`, order `60` |
| Locale namespace | `terminal-shell` |
| Bundle row id | `terminal-shell` |
| Host routes | `/api/dsh-terminal-shell/state`, `/api/dsh-terminal-shell/discover` |
| In-session tools | `bash` replaces `bash`, hides `pwsh`; `cmd` adds `cmd`, hides `pwsh` and `bash` (replaced session only) |

dsh-terminal-shell README · Coexisting with other plugins：- **Writes no global state** — no `ctx.shell`, no preset edits, nothing in the install dir, no pinned path. With `sidebarBash: gitbash` it hands the core `terminal-controller` an in-memory `config.shell` override (never persisted); `system` leaves it untouched.
- **Another plugin that also replaces the session's `bash`** (for example another Git Bash plugin): both want it; this plugin skips when it finds a `bash` already in scope (`already-replaced`) but cannot tell whose. Install just one.
